mechanism: GithubClaimLease.listComments calls /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{n}/comments?per_page=100 without handling pagination or Link headers. When an issue has >100 comments, the first 100 comments (page 1) fill the response. A boundary marker (abort/finish/park/stale_claim_removed) at index >= 100 and subsequent competing claims at index >= 100 (page 2+) are never seen by listComments. In GithubClaimWindow.of(), the comments parsed from page 1 contain none of the post-boundary claims or the boundary itself. For both racing claimers A and B whose comments are on page 2+, window.winnerAgainst(ownCommentId) finds no opposing claim in the window (and does not even see ownCommentId). winnerAgainst returns Optional.empty(), so neither claimer detects that it was beaten. Both claimers fall back to winnerId = ownCommentId and return ClaimResult.Acquired(new ClaimEpoch(ownCommentId)). Consequently, both claimers simultaneously conclude they acquired the lease on the same issue.
impact: CRITICAL: Mutual exclusion failure on tasks with >100 comments. Multiple factory workers concurrently execute the same task (split-brain execution), corrupting task state, racing on task branches, and issuing duplicate/conflicting actions.
